title: Reachable role management writes legacy global RBAC instead of tenant RBAC
currentBehavior: The roles pages call legacy settings actions that mutate roles and role_permissions, while runtime authorization resolves tenant_user_roles, tenant_roles, and tenant_role_permissions.
impact: A tenant admin can receive success feedback while active tenant permissions are unchanged, or can mutate global role templates from a tenant-facing page.
tenantSecurityRisk: Cross-tenant/global authorization metadata mutation and misleading success feedback.
downstreamObservation: Runtime permission checks do not observe the legacy role mutation as tenant permissions.
atomicity: Role permission replacement deletes and inserts outside a transaction.
zeroRowDetection: Legacy writes do not consistently prove tenant-canonical rows changed.
staleRaceHandling: Role replacement can temporarily remove all role permissions during concurrent reads.
missingTests: DB/action test proving roles UI mutates tenant RBAC tables observed by runtime permission lookup.
recommendedChange: Rewire tenant role pages to tenant-roles actions or move legacy role template management to a platform-only surface.
migrationImplication: Likely none for rewiring; data migration may be needed if legacy role templates must be copied to tenant roles.
rollback: Revert documentation/contract test; runtime fix rollback would restore old roles UI wiring.

title: Assignment planning and interest actions are not consistently tenant-bound
currentBehavior: Several helpers require permissions but fetch or mutate by assignment, round, or candidate id without first constraining the parent row to the current tenant.
impact: A user with valid backoffice permission and a known UUID may read, notify, recalculate, reschedule, or delete another tenant's assignment data.
tenantSecurityRisk: Foreign-tenant identifier existence and mutation risk.
downstreamObservation: Capacity persistence uses the assignment row's tenant and can therefore write cross-tenant candidates if the parent lookup is cross-tenant.
atomicity: Several planning side effects run outside a single tenant-bound transaction.
zeroRowDetection: Some deletes and updates do not use returned rows to fail closed.
staleRaceHandling: Pre-read plus later mutation patterns can race with deletion or tenant state changes.
missingTests: Runtime server-action tests with cross-tenant assignment and interest round ids.
recommendedChange: Require current tenant in every action and include tenant context in every parent and child query or prove it through a tenant-bound parent relation.
rollback: Revert action hardening if needed; no data rollback expected.

title: Generic assignment status editing can bypass lifecycle invariants
currentBehavior: Generic edit accepts status, and the status stepper can call setAssignmentStatus with allowAny true, bypassing normal transitions.
impact: Backoffice can produce customer-visible final states without required execution evidence, report approval, invoice readiness, or customer closeout artifacts.
tenantSecurityRisk: Tenant-bound status updates exist in setAssignmentStatus, but lifecycle integrity and downstream evidence are not enforced.
downstreamObservation: Customer portal observes assignment status directly.
atomicity: Status update, route refresh, audit, and downstream observation are separate.
zeroRowDetection: Status update does not verify the updated row through returning rows.
staleRaceHandling: Transition check uses a pre-read and can race with concurrent status changes.
missingTests: Runtime tests for final-state override requiring reason and closeout artifacts.
recommendedChange: Remove generic status from broad edit, require explicit transition commands, and require reason/authority for override states.
rollback: Revert status command changes if needed.

title: Report approval can commit without invoice proposal
currentBehavior: Report approval updates report and assignment status, then attempts invoice proposal creation in a try/catch. Proposal failure is logged while approval may still return success.
impact: Customer-visible approved reports can exist without the expected draft invoice proposal.
tenantSecurityRisk: Tenant filters are present on report lookup, but atomic canonical state is not guaranteed.
downstreamObservation: Customer portal can observe approved reports before finance state is complete.
atomicity: Report approval, assignment transition, invoice proposal, audit, and notifications are not one transaction.
zeroRowDetection: Status updates are not conditional on expected status with returned row proof.
staleRaceHandling: Concurrent approval/rejection can race after pre-read.
missingTests: DB integration test proving approval rolls back when proposal creation fails.
recommendedChange: Wrap approval, assignment transition, proposal creation, and audit in one transaction; emit notifications after commit.
migrationImplication: A future unique active-invoice constraint may require a new forward-only migration.
rollback: Revert transaction hardening; data repair may be needed for partial approved reports.

title: Customer portal signs raw document storage paths
currentBehavior: Customer portal document download filters the document row by tenant, then signs doc.storagePath directly. Backoffice uses a tenant-bound path helper before signing.
impact: A legacy or corrupt current-tenant document row with a foreign storage path could receive a signed URL.
tenantSecurityRisk: Storage path is not independently tenant-bound in the customer portal action.
downstreamObservation: Signed URL issuance is not audited in customer portal downloads.
atomicity: Signing is outside a DB transaction; audit is missing.
zeroRowDetection: The document row lookup detects not found, but storage path safety is not verified.
staleRaceHandling: No freshness check between row lookup and signed URL issuance.
missingTests: Customer portal signed URL test rejecting cross-tenant storage paths.
recommendedChange: Use the shared tenant-bound storage path helper before signing and write a sensitive access audit row.
rollback: Revert portal download helper change if needed.

title: Organization settings updates do not detect zero-row updates
currentBehavior: Settings updates are tenant-scoped but do not use returning rows or affected-row checks before returning success and writing audit.
impact: Provisioning drift can produce success feedback without committed settings state.
tenantSecurityRisk: Tenant predicate is present, but success is not tied to canonical mutation.
downstreamObservation: Mail, notification, logo, and template behavior may remain unchanged.
atomicity: Mutation and audit are separate.
zeroRowDetection: Missing.
staleRaceHandling: No row-version or returned-row proof.
missingTests: Runtime zero-row tests for settings update actions.
recommendedChange: Use update returning rows and fail recoverably when no tenant settings row exists, or perform an intentional upsert.
rollback: Revert settings mutation hardening.

title: SMTP secret storage is plaintext and legacy fallback is global
currentBehavior: Tenant SMTP password is stored in organization_settings.smtp_password as plaintext, while legacy SMTP fallback reads enabled rows globally.
impact: Database readers/backups expose tenant SMTP credentials; fallback transport selection can use another tenant's SMTP configuration.
tenantSecurityRisk: Secret confidentiality and tenant isolation risk.
downstreamObservation: Mail delivery may use unexpected sender settings.
atomicity: Secret write and audit are separate.
zeroRowDetection: Settings update zero-row issue also applies.
staleRaceHandling: No encrypted secret versioning.
missingTests: Secret-at-rest contract and tenant-scoped SMTP provider selection test.
recommendedChange: Encrypt tenant SMTP passwords with the same envelope pattern as provider config and remove global tenant SMTP fallback.
migrationImplication: Future fix likely needs a forward-only migration for encrypted SMTP secrets.
rollback: Runtime rollback must preserve readable legacy secrets until migration completes.

title: Backoffice audit log listing is not tenant-scoped
currentBehavior: listAuditLog requires settings read permission but does not require current tenant or filter auditLogTable.tenantId in the ultimate query.
impact: Tenant admins may view audit rows outside their tenant if table contents include cross-tenant rows.
tenantSecurityRisk: Cross-tenant audit metadata disclosure.
downstreamObservation: Audit UI can show entries unrelated to the current tenant.
atomicity: Read-only issue.
zeroRowDetection: Not applicable.
staleRaceHandling: Pagination can mix unrelated tenant rows.
missingTests: Tenant-scoped audit list query contract and runtime denial test.
recommendedChange: Require current tenant and filter audit rows by tenant, with platform-only separate audit surface.
migrationImplication: May require backfilling audit_log.tenant_id in future runtime work.
rollback: Revert query filter if platform audit access needs a separate path.

title: Notification audience options are not tenant-scoped
currentBehavior: getNotificationAudienceOptions queries active personnel and customers without requiring current tenant in the action.
impact: Manual notification audience selection can leak cross-tenant names or ids and enable misdirected notifications.
tenantSecurityRisk: Cross-tenant PII disclosure and notification targeting risk.
downstreamObservation: Manual notifications can be prepared for wrong audiences.
atomicity: Read-only list issue; send path needs separate runtime proof.
zeroRowDetection: Not applicable.
staleRaceHandling: Audience list can be stale between selection and send.
missingTests: Tenant-scoped notification audience list contract.
recommendedChange: Require current tenant and filter all personnel/customer audience queries by tenant.
rollback: Revert audience query hardening if a platform broadcast surface is added separately.

title: Customer, object, contact, and customer type mutations have scope and zero-row gaps
currentBehavior: Customer types are tenant-facing but globally mutable, and several customer/object/contact status/delete actions do not verify affected rows.
impact: One tenant can change shared customer type catalog behavior; stale ids can produce false success and audit rows.
tenantSecurityRisk: Global catalog mutation and misleading canonical success.
downstreamObservation: Customer filters/forms can show shared catalog changes across tenants.
atomicity: Primary contact demotion and write are not one transaction.
zeroRowDetection: Missing on several state-change actions.
staleRaceHandling: Concurrent primary-contact writes can leave multiple primaries.
missingTests: Runtime zero-row tests and tenant/global customer type decision test.
recommendedChange: Decide whether customer types are platform-global or tenant-scoped; add returning checks and transactional primary-contact writes.
migrationImplication: Tenant-scoped customer types or primary-contact uniqueness would require future migrations.
rollback: Revert catalog scope changes carefully if shared catalog is intended.

title: Document upload, delete, and parent deletion are not atomic across Storage and DB
currentBehavior: Upload writes Storage then DB then audit; delete removes Storage then DB then audit and ignores Storage remove errors. Customer/object delete does not clean generic document blobs/rows.
impact: Orphaned blobs, DB rows pointing to missing blobs, or retained sensitive files after parent deletion.
tenantSecurityRisk: Sensitive document retention and audit gap.
downstreamObservation: Portal may hide orphaned docs while Storage still retains files.
atomicity: Not atomic across Storage, DB, and audit.
zeroRowDetection: Storage delete result is ignored.
staleRaceHandling: Parent deletion can race with document upload/listing.
missingTests: Partial failure tests for upload/delete and parent delete with linked documents.
recommendedChange: Check Storage errors, use compensating cleanup, block parent deletion with documents or archive/delete documents with audit.
migrationImplication: Possible future FK/model migration if documents become strongly typed by parent.
rollback: Revert document lifecycle hardening; repair orphaned files manually if needed.

title: Customer portal document direct actions do not enforce documents module
currentBehavior: Customer portal layout gates the portal generally and desktop nav hides documents via flags, but document server actions and mobile route are not module-gated.
impact: Documents can remain reachable by direct URL or server action when the module is disabled.
tenantSecurityRisk: Module-off direct action bypass.
downstreamObservation: Hidden UI does not prove server-side denial.
atomicity: Read/download action issue.
zeroRowDetection: Not applicable.
staleRaceHandling: Module changes may not be reflected in direct action calls.
missingTests: Portal direct-action module-off denial for documents.
recommendedChange: Add customer portal module guard in getMyDocuments and getDocumentDownloadUrl and filter mobile routes.
rollback: Revert portal module gate if product policy changes.

title: Personnel PWA availability and leave actions lack action-level tenant and settings scope
currentBehavior: Layout checks portal tenant, but actions resolve personnel by user id and read first organization settings row without tenant scope.
impact: Direct action calls can bypass host/module tenant checks; availability horizon or leave notification recipient can come from another tenant.
tenantSecurityRisk: Cross-tenant personnel record and settings risk.
downstreamObservation: Backoffice planning may observe availability written under wrong assumptions.
atomicity: Availability replace flows are not transactional.
zeroRowDetection: Several updates/deletes lack returning checks.
staleRaceHandling: Leave approve/reject can race after pre-read.
missingTests: PWA direct action tenant/module runtime denial tests.
recommendedChange: Require current personnel portal tenant inside actions and filter personnel/settings by tenant.
rollback: Revert PWA tenant guard changes if needed.

title: Qualification links do not prove referenced records are same-tenant
currentBehavior: Personnel row tenant is validated, but qualification, role, and task-code references are not all tenant-validated before link writes.
impact: Known or leaked UUIDs can create cross-tenant qualification/task references.
tenantSecurityRisk: Linked child entities are not fully tenant-bound.
downstreamObservation: Planning and suitability can use polluted qualifications.
atomicity: Normalized link writes and legacy field sync are separate.
zeroRowDetection: Referenced row absence or tenant mismatch is not always detected before write.
staleRaceHandling: Legacy sync can diverge from normalized links.
missingTests: Cross-tenant qualification id runtime tests.
recommendedChange: Validate every referenced qualification, role, and task code against current tenant before writing links.
migrationImplication: Future composite FK or uniqueness constraints may need migration.
rollback: Revert link validation if needed.

title: Availability replace and leave decisions are non-atomic and race-prone
currentBehavior: Weekly availability deletes then inserts outside a transaction. Leave approve/reject selects pending status first, then updates by id.
impact: Partial availability deletion or simultaneous approve/reject can both appear successful and send conflicting notifications.
tenantSecurityRisk: Tenant predicates exist in backoffice leave paths, but canonical success is not reliable under races.
downstreamObservation: Planning can consume partial or stale availability.
atomicity: Missing for replace flows and leave decision side effects.
zeroRowDetection: Missing in several update/delete actions.
staleRaceHandling: Expected pending status is not part of the update predicate.
missingTests: Concurrent leave approve/reject and partial availability failure tests.
recommendedChange: Use transactions, status predicates, returning checks, and recoverable conflict errors.
rollback: Revert transaction hardening if needed.

title: requiredPersonnelCount is not enforced in scheduling write paths
currentBehavior: UI displays requiredPersonnelCount, but scheduling/direct assignment computes required slots from required roles and falls back to 1.
impact: Multi-person assignments can be under-filled and marked scheduled.
tenantSecurityRisk: No direct cross-tenant issue, but tenant operational state becomes false.
downstreamObservation: Personnel and customer portals may observe scheduled state before staffing is complete.
atomicity: Assignment link and status transition are separate.
zeroRowDetection: Link/status updates need returning checks.
staleRaceHandling: Concurrent assign/unassign can race with auto-schedule.
missingTests: Behavioral test for requiredPersonnelCount greater than required role count.
recommendedChange: Use Math.max(requiredPersonnelCount, requiredRoleIds.length, 1) consistently in capacity and scheduling mutations.
rollback: Revert capacity calculation change if needed.

title: Selected interest candidates are not actual assigned personnel
currentBehavior: Selecting a candidate marks an interest response selected, but does not create assignment_personnel.status assigned.
impact: Planner can interpret selected as assigned while personnel execution views do not show executable work.
tenantSecurityRisk: State-model ambiguity can cause missed work or incorrect manual follow-up.
downstreamObservation: Personnel PWA lists assigned work from assignment_personnel, not selected interest responses.
atomicity: Selection and assignment are separate concepts with no promotion transaction.
zeroRowDetection: Candidate marking should verify affected rows.
staleRaceHandling: Candidate availability can be stale between poll response and selection.
missingTests: E2E/action test proving selected-only candidates do not appear in execution lists.
recommendedChange: Clarify copy and state model or explicitly promote selected candidates through a real assignment action.
rollback: Revert UI wording or promotion behavior if needed.

title: Multi-person execution uses global assignment status
currentBehavior: Any linked assigned worker can move the shared assignment status through en route, in progress, completed, or not completed.
impact: One worker can prematurely complete or fail a team assignment for everyone, with customer-visible impact.
tenantSecurityRisk: Tenant-bound membership may be checked, but actor authority within a team is not modeled.
downstreamObservation: Customer portal observes the global assignment status.
atomicity: Per-person and global state are not separated.
zeroRowDetection: Some PWA status updates do not verify returned rows.
staleRaceHandling: Concurrent workers can race to final states.
missingTests: Multi-person execution quorum/lead-worker tests.
recommendedChange: Introduce per-person execution state or explicit lead/quorum rules before global finalization.
migrationImplication: Likely future schema migration if per-person execution state is introduced.
rollback: Runtime rollback would need compatibility for existing global statuses.

title: Stale planning candidates can remain visible
currentBehavior: Capacity persistence upserts current candidates but does not delete candidates absent from the latest calculation; board reads stored candidates without freshness filtering.
impact: Planner can see suggested personnel who are no longer eligible or available.
tenantSecurityRisk: Stale suggestions can leak outdated suitability context within a tenant.
downstreamObservation: Suggested personnel is not the same as assigned personnel.
atomicity: Recalculation and stale cleanup are not one operation.
zeroRowDetection: Stale rows are not detected or removed.
staleRaceHandling: No latest capacity-check id guards reads.
missingTests: Recalculation test where removed/inactive personnel disappears from candidates.
recommendedChange: Delete candidates not present in the latest result or key candidate reads to a latest capacity check id.
migrationImplication: none expected unless latest-check versioning is added.
rollback: Revert stale cleanup behavior if needed.

title: Invoice, report, material, and inventory transitions are race-prone
currentBehavior: Invoice proposal creation checks then inserts without a uniqueness guard; multiple transitions pre-read status and update without expected-status returning checks.
impact: Duplicate active proposals, false success transitions, and report approval recovery gaps.
tenantSecurityRisk: Tenant predicates are often present, but canonical finance state can diverge.
downstreamObservation: Customer-visible reports and invoice status may diverge from internal finance readiness.
atomicity: Several transitions and audits are separate.
zeroRowDetection: Missing on multiple transitions.
staleRaceHandling: Expected status is not consistently part of update predicates.
missingTests: Concurrent proposal creation and zero-row transition tests.
recommendedChange: Add conditional updates with returning checks and a partial unique active-invoice constraint in a future permitted migration.
migrationImplication: Future partial unique index migration likely required.
rollback: Runtime rollback must handle duplicate proposal compatibility.

title: Ticket resources are not mapped to module entitlements
currentBehavior: Backoffice ticket actions require RBAC permission for tickets, but tickets is not mapped to a module entitlement; customer portal support links are unconditional.
impact: Tenants with notifications/tickets disabled can still reach ticket reads or mutations through direct actions.
tenantSecurityRisk: Module-off direct action bypass.
downstreamObservation: Hidden navigation does not prove server-side denial.
atomicity: Not applicable to read/write gate itself.
zeroRowDetection: Ticket mutations have separate zero-row issues.
staleRaceHandling: Module changes may not invalidate direct actions.
missingTests: Runtime module-off ticket and notification action denial tests.
recommendedChange: Map ticket/message resources to the notifications module or add explicit module checks in all ticket/notification actions.
rollback: Revert module map change if product entitlement model changes.

title: Ticket writes and downstream event/audit writes are not atomic
currentBehavior: Ticket/message rows commit before emitDomainEvent. Event, audit, notifications, and queue rows are written in separate statements.
impact: Durable ticket mutations can exist without downstream event, audit, queue, or notification records.
tenantSecurityRisk: Auditability and notification observability are not guaranteed.
downstreamObservation: Backoffice and portal notifications can miss committed state.
atomicity: Missing between canonical mutation and downstream effects.
zeroRowDetection: Event/audit writes do not repair already committed ticket mutations on failure.
staleRaceHandling: Retries can duplicate user-visible messages or events.
missingTests: Outbox/event atomicity tests and retry/idempotency tests.
recommendedChange: Use an outbox written in the same transaction as the ticket mutation or track repairable event delivery state.
migrationImplication: Future outbox table or constraints may need migration.
rollback: Runtime rollback must preserve event delivery compatibility.

title: General personnel tickets do not emit cross-surface events
currentBehavior: General personnel ticket create/reply writes local thread/message state and revalidates routes, but does not emit a domain event. Assignment questions and customer tickets do emit events.
impact: Backoffice consumers may not observe ordinary personnel tickets until manual/list refresh.
tenantSecurityRisk: Audit and notification gap for personnel communications.
downstreamObservation: No domain event for general personnel ticket create/reply.
atomicity: No event is produced; local transaction only covers rows.
zeroRowDetection: Reply/update paths need row proof.
staleRaceHandling: Manual refresh required for observation.
missingTests: Cross-surface event contract for personnel ticket create/reply.
recommendedChange: Emit tenant-bound personnel_ticket_created and personnel_ticket_replied events with audit metadata.
migrationImplication: none expected if event keys are code-only.
rollback: Revert event emission if downstream consumers are not ready.

title: Notification and portal ticket actions can hide server failures
currentBehavior: Single-row notification updates do not check affected rows, and portal UIs ignore some action results while optimistically changing local state.
impact: Stale, deleted, or unauthorized ids can look successful and leave UI diverged from canonical state.
tenantSecurityRisk: Errors are not visible or recoverable.
downstreamObservation: Local UI state can differ from server state.
atomicity: Single-row mutation and UI update are not tied to committed state proof.
zeroRowDetection: Missing.
staleRaceHandling: No recoverable stale-data response.
missingTests: Zero-row notification mutation and portal error rendering tests.
recommendedChange: Return failure on zero-row single mutations and only update UI/revalidate on success.
rollback: Revert UI error handling if needed.

title: Platform exports and ticket audits miss actual mutation/download proof
currentBehavior: CSV routes are gated but do not audit actual downloads; platform ticket update writes audit after an update without returned row proof.
impact: Compliance trail can miss exports or contain mutation audits for rows that did not change.
tenantSecurityRisk: Auditability gap; platform scope rather than tenant runtime.
downstreamObservation: Audit log does not prove download occurrence.
atomicity: Mutation/download and audit are separate.
zeroRowDetection: Missing for some platform ticket updates.
staleRaceHandling: Race/deletion can produce false audit success.
missingTests: Export download audit and platform ticket zero-row tests.
recommendedChange: Write audit rows after successful CSV generation and use returning checks for platform ticket mutations.
rollback: Revert audit additions if needed.

title: Auto-invite feedback can overstate committed notification state
currentBehavior: createPersonnel can swallow auto-invite failure, while UI copy says a temporary password was sent when autoInvite is selected.
impact: Backoffice user can believe portal access was sent when only the personnel row exists.
tenantSecurityRisk: Notification success is conflated with canonical personnel creation.
downstreamObservation: Personnel may not receive access despite success copy.
atomicity: Personnel create and invite delivery are not atomic.
zeroRowDetection: Not the main issue.
staleRaceHandling: Invite failure has no visible retry state.
missingTests: Action/UI test separating created from invite sent.
recommendedChange: Return invite status separately and show recoverable retry path.
rollback: Revert feedback split if needed.

title: Route and map side effects are best-effort and unevenly triggered
currentBehavior: Route refresh and realtime invalidation failures are swallowed. removePersonnel refreshes routes, but a planning-board unassign path does not clearly refresh route contexts.
impact: Assignment changes can commit while maps/routes remain stale.
tenantSecurityRisk: Operational reliability risk rather than direct tenant leakage.
downstreamObservation: Route/map surfaces can lag behind assignment-personnel changes.
atomicity: Route refresh is outside canonical mutation.
zeroRowDetection: Side-effect failures are logged but not surfaced.
staleRaceHandling: Best-effort invalidation can race with route reads.
missingTests: Mutation-side route refresh coverage for all assign/unassign paths.
recommendedChange: Refresh/invalidate routes from all assignment-personnel link mutations and surface non-blocking warnings where needed.
rollback: Revert route side-effect additions if needed.
